itinerary.cal: Cascade River Road typically opens for the season in late May/June and the upper basin can hold snow into July, so verify current conditions before a bushwhack approach.

days.note: Start on the maintained Cascade Pass Trail, then continue past the pass toward Pelton Basin before dropping off-trail into the Trapper Lake basin. The final descent to the lake is an unmaintained fisherman's path that loses itself quickly and turns into a steep, brushy bushwhack, so budget extra time and daylight for route-finding.
days.title: Approach via Cascade Pass to Trapper Lake camp

schedule.label: Leave Cascade River Road trailhead
schedule.detail: Popular trail, ~3.7 mi and 1,800 ft to Cascade Pass.

schedule.label: Enter Pelton Basin area
schedule.detail: Leave the beaten path and start angling toward the Trapper Lake drainage.

schedule.label: Begin bushwhack descent to Trapper Lake
schedule.detail: Steep, brushy, and reportedly longer than it looks; losing and regaining the fisherman's path is common.

schedule.label: Make camp near Trapper Lake
schedule.detail: ~5,000 ft basin below the peak's south side.

days.objective: Reach a basin camp near Trapper Lake

days.note: From the lake camp, work up open slopes and heather/talus benches on the mountain's south side to the summit, then reverse the same line. This is the standard non-technical line up the peak (no pitches), but expect loose rock and possible lingering snow patches depending on season.
days.title: South Slopes summit push

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light alpine-start pack; carry an ice axe if snow lingers on the upper slopes.

schedule.label: Gain the south ridge/upper slopes
schedule.detail: Terrain steepens into looser talus and broken rock benches.

schedule.label: Summit (7,530 ft)
schedule.detail: Views across the Glacier Peak Wilderness / North Cascades NP boundary.

schedule.label: Reverse the South Slopes
schedule.detail: Downclimb the ascent line, watching for loosened rock kicked from above.

schedule.label: Back at Trapper Lake camp
schedule.detail: Rest, refill water, dry gear for the hike out.

days.objective: Climb Trapper Mountain (7,530 ft) via the South Slopes and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the bushwhack back up out of the Trapper Lake basin to the Pelton Basin area, rejoin the Cascade Pass Trail, and hike out over the pass to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Cascade River Road trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 3-day trip (~19 mi, ~5,800 ft round-trip gain) built around a genuine off-trail bushwhack to Trapper Lake — not a car-to-car outing.

climate.fall: Shortening weather windows; snow can return to the high country by October.
climate.spring: Deep, lingering snowpack; Cascade Pass and Pelton Basin are typically snow-covered and NPS will not issue backcountry reservations for trips starting before July 1.
climate.summer: The best and most reliable climbing window, July through September.
climate.winter: Cascade River Road is closed at mile 20; the peak is effectively inaccessible except to ski/snowshoe mountaineers.
climate.typical: Marine-influenced North Cascades climate with a strong crest effect: heavy winter snowpack, wet springs, and a relatively dry, sunny summer window. Because the peak sits near the range crest close to Cascade Pass, weather can build quickly from the west even on an otherwise clear day.

bySeason.fall: Snow can return to the high basins by late September/October, complicated by shortened daylight.
bySeason.spring: Heavy lingering snowpack, high stream crossings below Pelton Basin, and difficult access make spring a poor season for this route.
bySeason.summer: July-September is the reliable weather and access window; warm days with cold nights at Trapper Lake (~5,000 ft) and cooler conditions near the 7,530 ft summit, plus afternoon thunderstorm risk by late summer.
bySeason.winter: Effectively inaccessible — Cascade River Road is closed well below the trailhead and the trails are snowed in.

climate.forecastZone: Outside NWAC's routine avalanche-forecast coverage; the closest usable proxy zones are NWAC's East Slopes Central and NWS Cascades-East mountain weather forecasts, but treat both as approximations for this Stehekin-side terrain.
